sentences.zh: 【宋紀八】 起重光單閼，盡玄黓執徐，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 8] From Chongguang danyue through Xuanyi zhixu; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 8] From Chongguang danyue through Xuanyi zhixu—a span of two years.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝下之上元嘉二十八年（

translations.literal: Upper portion of the Annals of Taizu the Literary Emperor, Yuanjia year twenty-eight (
translations.idiomatic: From the upper section of the reign of Emperor Wen, the Literary Emperor—Yuanjia, year twenty-eight (

sentences.zh: 辛卯，公元四五一年）

translations.literal: xinmao, CE 451)
translations.idiomatic: xinmao, 451 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙戌朔，魏主大會群臣於瓜步山上，班爵行賞有差。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the bingxu new moon, the Wei ruler held a great assembly of his civil and military officials on Mount Guabu and distributed ranks and rewards in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (bingxu), the Wei emperor gathered his ministers on Mount Guabu and conferred titles and rewards according to merit.

sentences.zh: 魏人緣江舉火；

translations.literal: The Wei men lit fires along the river;
translations.idiomatic: Along the riverbank, the Wei troops kindled bonfires;

sentences.zh: 太子石衛率尹弘言於上曰：「六夷如此，必走。」

translations.literal: Yin Hong, a guard of the Crown Prince's household, said to the Emperor: "The six barbarians are acting thus—they are certain to flee."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hong, an attendant of the Crown Prince's guard, told the emperor, "The northerners are behaving this way—they will surely withdraw."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏掠居民、焚廬舍而去。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Wei looted the inhabitants, burned the cottages, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Wei raiders seized civilians, burned the homes, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 故誕世之反也，江夏王義恭等奏彭城王義康數有怨言，搖動民聽，故不逞之族因以生心，請徙義康廣州。

translations.literal: Because of Liu Dan's rebellion, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, and others memorialized that the Prince of Pengcheng, Yikang, had repeatedly uttered complaints, unsettling popular opinion, so that unruly factions had thereby gained heart; they requested that Yikang be relocated to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of Liu Dan's revolt, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and others reported that Prince Yikang of Pengcheng had voiced repeated grievances that stirred public sentiment, giving malcontents an opening; they asked that Yikang be exiled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上將徙義康，先遣使語之，義康曰：「人生會死，吾豈愛生！

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to relocate Yikang and first sent an envoy to inform him. Yikang said: "Human life must end—how could I cling to life!
translations.idiomatic: Before relocating Yikang, the emperor sent an envoy to tell him. Yikang replied, "Everyone must die someday—do you think I cling to life?

sentences.zh: 必為亂階，雖遠何益！

translations.literal: I am bound to become a source of rebellion—what good would distance do!
translations.idiomatic: I will surely become a pretext for rebellion—what good is exile?

sentences.zh: 請死於此，恥復屢遷。」

translations.literal: I ask to die here; I am ashamed to be moved again and again."
translations.idiomatic: Let me die here—I am ashamed to be uprooted yet again."

sentences.zh: 竟未及往。

translations.literal: In the end he had not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never made the journey.

sentences.zh: 魏師之瓜步，人情忷懼。

translations.literal: When the Wei army reached Guabu, popular sentiment was agitated with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei army advanced to Guabu, the populace was seized with panic.

sentences.zh: 上慮不逞之人復奉義康為亂；

translations.literal: The Emperor feared that unruly persons might again rally behind Yikang to make trouble;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried that malcontents might again rally behind Yikang to foment rebellion;

sentences.zh: 太子劭及武陵王駿、尚書左僕射何尚之屢啟宜早為之所；

translations.literal: the Crown Prince Shao, the Prince of Wuling, Jun, and the Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, He Shangzhi, repeatedly urged that he should be dealt with early;
translations.idiomatic: the Crown Prince Shao, Prince Jun of Wuling, and He Shangzhi, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, repeatedly urged swift action;

sentences.zh: 上乃遣中書舍人嚴龍繼藥賜義康死。

translations.literal: the Emperor then sent the Secretariat Attendant Yan Long with poison to grant Yikang death.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor then sent Yan Long, a Secretariat attendant, with poison to order Yikang's death.

sentences.zh: 義康不肯服，曰：「佛教不許自殺；

translations.literal: Yikang refused to take it and said: "Buddhism does not permit suicide;
translations.idiomatic: Yikang refused the poison and said, "Buddhism forbids suicide;

sentences.zh: 願隨宜處分。」

translations.literal: I wish that you dispose of me as you see fit."
translations.idiomatic: do with me as you will."

sentences.zh: 使者以被掩殺之。

translations.literal: The envoy smothered him with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy smothered him with a quilt instead.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭以碻磝不可守，召王玄謨還歷城；

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, judged that Que'ao could not be held and summoned Wang Xuemo back to Licheng;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia decided Que'ao was indefensible and recalled Wang Xuemo to Licheng;

sentences.zh: 魏人追擊敗之，遂取碻磝。

translations.literal: the Wei pursued, defeated him, and thereupon took Que'ao.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei pursued, routed his force, and seized Que'ao.

sentences.zh: 初，上聞魏將入寇，命廣陵太守劉懷之逆燒城府、船乘，盡帥其民渡江。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor heard that the Wei were about to invade, he ordered the Administrator of Guangling, Liu Huaizhi, to burn the government offices and vessels in advance and to lead all his people across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on word that the Wei were invading, the emperor ordered Liu Huaizhi, Administrator of Guangling, to burn the government offices and ships beforehand and lead the entire population south across the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 山陽太守蕭僧珍悉斂其民入城，台送糧仗詣盱眙及滑台者，以路不通，皆留山陽；

translations.literal: the Administrator of Shanyang, Xiao Sengzhen, gathered all his people into the city; grain and weapons sent from the capital for Xuyi and Huatai, because the roads were blocked, were all kept at Shanyang;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sengzhen, Administrator of Shanyang, gathered everyone into the city; supplies bound for Xuyi and Huatai from the capital were all held at Shanyang because the roads were cut;

sentences.zh: 蓄陂水令滿，須魏人至，決以灌之。

translations.literal: he stored up the reservoir water until it was full, intending when the Wei arrived to breach it and flood them.
translations.idiomatic: he filled the reservoir and planned to breach the dam and flood the Wei when they arrived.

sentences.zh: 魏人過山陽，不敢留，因攻盱眙。

translations.literal: The Wei passed through Shanyang, dared not linger, and therefore attacked Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei passed through Shanyang without stopping and pressed on to besiege Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 魏主就臧質求酒，質封溲便與之；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler asked Zang Zhi for wine; Zhi sealed urine in a vessel and sent it to him;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor asked Zang Zhi for wine; Zhi sent him a sealed jar of urine instead;

sentences.zh: 魏主怒，築長圍，一夕而合；

translations.literal: the Wei ruler was enraged, built a long encirclement, and closed it in a single night;
translations.idiomatic: enraged, the Wei emperor threw up a siege line that closed in a single night;

sentences.zh: 運東山土石以填塹，作浮橋於君山，絕水陸道。

translations.literal: he transported earth and stone from East Hill to fill the moat and built a pontoon bridge at Jun Hill, cutting off both water and land routes.
translations.idiomatic: he hauled earth and stone from East Hill to fill the moat, built a pontoon bridge at Jun Hill, and severed both land and water access to the city.

sentences.zh: 魏主遺質書曰：「吾今所遣鬥兵，盡非我國人，城東北是丁零與胡，南是氐、羌。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler sent Zhi a letter saying: "The fighting troops I have now sent are none of them men of my own state. Northeast of the city are Dingling and Hu; south are Di and Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor wrote to Zhi: "The troops I have sent to fight are none of them my own people. Northeast of your city are Dingling and Hu; to the south are Di and Qiang.

sentences.zh: 設使丁零死，正可減常山、趙郡賊；

translations.literal: If the Dingling should die, that would only reduce the bandits of Changshan and Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: If the Dingling die, you only reduce the rebels of Changshan and Zhao;

sentences.zh: 胡死，減并州賊；

translations.literal: if the Hu die, that would reduce the bandits of Bing;
translations.idiomatic: if the Hu die, you reduce the rebels of Bing;

sentences.zh: 氐、羌死，減關中賊。

translations.literal: if the Di and Qiang die, that would reduce the bandits of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: if the Di and Qiang die, you reduce the rebels of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 卿若殺之，無所不利。」

translations.literal: If you kill them, you lose nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Slay them and you lose nothing."

sentences.zh: 質復書曰：「省示，具悉奸懷。

translations.literal: Zhi replied: "I have read your message and fully understand your treacherous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wrote back: "I have read your message and see your treacherous intent plainly.

sentences.zh: 爾自恃四足，屢犯邊境。

translations.literal: You rely on your four legs and have repeatedly violated our borders.
translations.idiomatic: You beasts on four legs have raided our borders again and again.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨退於東，申坦散於西，爾知其所以然邪？

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo retreated in the east and Shen Tan dispersed in the west—do you know why this was so?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo withdrew in the east and Shen Tan broke up in the west—do you know why?

sentences.zh: 爾獨不聞童謠之言乎？

translations.literal: Have you alone not heard what the children's rhyme says?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not heard the children's rhyme?

sentences.zh: 蓋卯年未至，故以二軍開飲江之路耳；

translations.literal: It is because the mao year has not yet arrived, and so the two armies were sent merely to open the road for drinking the river;
translations.idiomatic: The mao year has not yet come—that is why the two armies were sent only to open the road for drinking the Yangtze;

sentences.zh: 冥期使然，非復人事。

translations.literal: the dark appointed time makes it so—it is no longer a matter of human agency.
translations.idiomatic: fate ordains it—this is no longer within human control.

sentences.zh: 寡人受命相滅，期之白登，師行未遠。

translations.literal: I have received the mandate to destroy you; the rendezvous is at Baideng, and the army has not marched far.
translations.idiomatic: I have received the mandate to destroy you; we shall meet at Baideng, and our army has scarcely set out.

sentences.zh: 爾自送死，豈容復令爾生全，饗有桑干哉！

translations.literal: You deliver yourselves to death—how could I again let you leave alive and feast on the Sanggan!
translations.idiomatic: You march to your own deaths—how could I let you survive to feast on the Sanggan again!

sentences.zh: 爾有幸得為亂兵所殺，不幸則生相鎖縛，載以一驢，直送都市耳。

translations.literal: If you are fortunate you will be killed by the disorderly troops; if unfortunate you will be taken alive, bound in chains, loaded on a donkey, and sent straight to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: If you are lucky you will die in the rout; if not, you will be taken alive in chains, loaded on a donkey, and hauled straight to the capital.

sentences.zh: 我本圖全，若天地無靈，力屈於爾，齏之，粉之，屠之，裂之，猶未足以謝本朝。

translations.literal: I originally intended to spare you; if Heaven and Earth are without spirit and I am overcome by you, to mince you, powder you, slaughter you, and rend you would still not suffice to answer to our dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to spare you; but if Heaven and Earth fail me and I fall to you, even to mince, powder, slaughter, and rend you would not suffice to atone to our dynasty.

sentences.zh: 爾智識及眾力，豈能勝苻堅邪！

translations.literal: Can your wisdom and the strength of your masses surpass Fu Jian!
translations.idiomatic: Do you imagine your wits and numbers can surpass Fu Jian!

sentences.zh: 今春雨已降，兵方四集，爾但安意攻城，勿遽走！

translations.literal: Now the spring rains have fallen and troops are gathering from all four directions; you need only set your mind at ease on besieging the city—do not flee in haste!
translations.idiomatic: The spring rains have come and armies are converging from every quarter—settle in for the siege and do not flee in haste!

sentences.zh: 糧食乏者可見語，當出廩相貽。

translations.literal: Those short of grain may speak up—I shall send out from the granary to bestow on you.
translations.idiomatic: If you run short of grain, say so—I will send supplies from our granaries.

sentences.zh: 得所送劍刀，欲令我揮之爾身邪！」

translations.literal: You received the swords and blades I sent—do you wish me to wield them upon your persons!"
translations.idiomatic: You received the swords and blades I sent—do you want me to use them on you personally!"

sentences.zh: 魏主大怒，作鐵床，於其上施鐵鑱，曰：「破城得質，當坐之此上。」

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was greatly enraged, made an iron bed, and fitted it with iron spikes, saying: "When the city is taken and Zhi is captured, he shall be seated upon this."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor flew into a rage, had an iron bed made with iron spikes on it, and declared, "When the city falls and we take Zhi, he shall sit on this."

sentences.zh: 質又與魏眾書曰：「爾語虜中諸士庶：佛狸見與書，相待如此。

translations.literal: Zhi also wrote to the Wei masses: "Tell all the gentry and commoners among the barbarians: Folai's treatment of me in his letters has been thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi also wrote to the Wei troops: "Tell all the officers and commoners in the enemy camp: this is how Folai has treated me in his letters.

sentences.zh: 爾等正朔之民，何為自取縻滅，豈可不知轉禍為福邪！」

translations.literal: You are people of the true calendar—why do you bring bondage and destruction on yourselves? Can you not know how to turn misfortune into fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: You are subjects of the true calendar—why court ruin and captivity? Do you not know how to turn disaster to your advantage!"

sentences.zh: 並寫台格以與之云：「斬佛狸首，封萬戶侯，賜布、絹各萬匹。」

translations.literal: He also copied the court reward schedule and sent it to them, saying: "Whoever cuts off Folai's head shall be enfeoffed as Marquis of Ten Thousand Households and granted ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk."
translations.idiomatic: He copied the court's reward schedule and circulated it: "Whoever brings Folai's head shall be enfeoffed as Marquis of Ten Thousand Households and receive ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk."

sentences.zh: 魏人以鉤車鉤城樓，城內系以驅緪，數百人唱呼引之，車不能退。

translations.literal: The Wei used hook-carts to hook the city towers; inside the city they tied great ropes, and several hundred men chanted and hauled, so that the carts could not be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei deployed hook-carts to snag the city towers; defenders tied heavy ropes inside the wall, and hundreds of men hauled and chanted in unison until the carts could not be pulled back.

sentences.zh: 既夜，縋桶懸卒出，截其鉤，獲之。

translations.literal: When night came, they lowered buckets on ropes and sent soldiers out to cut off the hooks and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: That night they lowered buckets on ropes, sent men out to cut the hooks, and seized them.

sentences.zh: 明日，又以沖車攻城，城土堅密，每至，頹落不過數升。

translations.literal: The next day they again used battering rams against the city; the earth of the walls was firm and dense, and each time they struck, no more than a few sheng crumbled away.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they brought up battering rams again; the walls were so firm that each blow dislodged only a few handfuls of earth.

sentences.zh: 魏人乃肉薄登城，分番相代，墜而復升，莫有退者，殺傷萬計，屍與城平。

translations.literal: The Wei then pressed close and climbed the walls, relieving one another in shifts; those who fell rose again, and none retreated. The killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands, and the corpses were level with the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei then stormed the walls at close quarters, rotating assault teams in shifts; men who fell climbed again, and none retreated. Casualties ran into the tens of thousands, and the dead piled level with the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 凡攻之三旬，不拔。

translations.literal: In all they attacked for thirty days and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The assault lasted thirty days in all, yet the city did not fall.

sentences.zh: 會魏軍中多疾疫，或告以建康遣水軍自海入淮，又敕彭城斷其歸路；

translations.literal: It happened that pestilence was widespread in the Wei army, and some reported that Jiankang had sent a naval force from the sea into the Huai, while orders had also been issued at Pengcheng to cut off their line of retreat;
translations.idiomatic: Pestilence swept the Wei camp, and word came that Jiankang had dispatched a fleet from the sea into the Huai, while Pengcheng had been ordered to cut off their retreat;

sentences.zh: 二月，丙辰朔，魏主燒攻具退走。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the bingchen new moon, the Wei ruler burned his siege equipment and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the bingchen new moon, the Wei emperor burned his siege equipment and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 盱眙人欲追之，沈璞曰：「今兵不多，雖可固守，不可出戰；

translations.literal: The people of Xuyi wished to pursue them. Shen Pu said: "Our troops are few now; though we can hold firm, we cannot go out to give battle;
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xuyi wanted to pursue. Shen Pu said, "We have few troops; we can hold the city, but we cannot sally out to fight;

sentences.zh: 但整舟楫，示若欲北渡者，以速其走，計不須實行也。」

translations.literal: only put the boats and oars in order and show as if intending to cross north, to hasten their flight—the plan need not actually be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: only ready the boats and feign a crossing north to hurry them on their way—the plan need not actually be executed."

sentences.zh: 臧質以璞城主，使之上露板，璞固辭，歸功於質。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi, because Pu was lord of the city, had him ascend the dew-reporting board; Pu firmly declined and attributed the merit to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi, recognizing Pu as the city's defender, had him submit the victory report; Pu firmly declined and credited Zhi instead.

sentences.zh: 上聞，益嘉之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he praised him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he praised Pu all the more.

sentences.zh: 魏師過彭城，江夏王義恭震懼不敢擊。

translations.literal: When the Wei army passed Pengcheng, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, was shaken with fear and dared not strike.
translations.idiomatic: As the Wei army passed Pengcheng, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was too terrified to attack.

sentences.zh: 或告「虜驅南口萬餘，夕應宿安王陂，去城數十里，今追之，可悉得。」

translations.literal: Someone reported: "The barbarians are driving more than ten thousand people from the southern passes; this evening they should encamp at the Prince of An's Mound, several tens of li from the city—if we pursue now, we can take them all."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported, "The enemy is driving more than ten thousand captives from the south; tonight they should camp at Prince An's Mound, a few tens of li from the city—pursue now and we can recover them all."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆請行，義恭禁不許。

translations.literal: All the generals requested to go, but Yigong forbade it and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals begged to go, but Yigong refused permission.

sentences.zh: 明日，驛使至，上敕義恭悉力急追。

translations.literal: The next day a courier arrived, and the Emperor ordered Yigong to pursue with all his strength in haste.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a courier arrived with orders from the emperor commanding Yigong to pursue with all speed.

sentences.zh: 魏師已遠，義恭乃遣鎮軍司馬檀和之向蕭城。

translations.literal: The Wei army was already far off, and Yigong then sent the Army Marshal of the Pacification Force, Tan Hezhi, toward Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army was already far away; only then did Yigong send Tan Hezhi, Army Marshal of the Pacification Force, toward Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 魏人先已聞之。

translations.literal: The Wei had already heard of it beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei had already gotten wind of it.

sentences.zh: 盡殺所驅者而去。

translations.literal: They killed all those they had been driving and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They slaughtered all the captives they had been driving and marched on.

sentences.zh: 程天祚逃歸。

translations.literal: Cheng Tianzuo fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tianzuo escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 魏人凡破南兗、徐、兗、豫、青、冀六州，殺掠不可勝計，丁壯者即加斬截，嬰兒貫於槊上，盤舞以為戲。

translations.literal: The Wei in all broke the six provinces of Southern Yan, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Ji; the killing and plunder were beyond counting. Able-bodied men were immediately cut down; infants were strung on spears and whirled in dance for sport.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei overran the six provinces of Southern Yan, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Ji; the slaughter and plunder were beyond reckoning. Able-bodied men were cut down on the spot; infants were impaled on spears and spun about for amusement.

sentences.zh: 所過郡縣，赤地無餘，春燕歸，巢於林木。

translations.literal: In the commanderies and counties they passed, the land was bare to the last trace; when the spring swallows returned, they nested in the trees.
translations.idiomatic: Every county and commandery they passed was left utterly bare; when the spring swallows returned, they nested in the woods.

sentences.zh: 魏之士馬死傷亦過半，國人皆尤之。

translations.literal: Wei soldiers and horses also suffered casualties of more than half, and the people of the state all blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei casualties among men and horses also exceeded half, and the people of the state all blamed the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上每命將出師，常授以成律，交戰日時，亦待中詔，是以將帥趑趄，莫敢自決。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor ordered generals to take the field, he always gave them fixed regulations; the day and hour of engagement also awaited an imperial edict from the center, and so the commanders hesitated and dared not decide for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor sent generals into the field, he gave them rigid battle plans; even the day and hour of engagement awaited a central edict, so commanders hesitated and dared not act on their own.

sentences.zh: 又江南白丁，輕進易退，此其所以敗也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the common conscripts of Jiangnan advance lightly and retreat easily—this is why they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jiangnan's raw conscripts advance rashly and retreat readily—this is why they were defeated.

sentences.zh: 自是邑裡蕭條，元嘉之政衰矣。

translations.literal: From this time the towns and hamlets were desolate, and the governance of the Yuanjia era declined.
translations.idiomatic: From this point towns and villages lay in ruin, and the prosperity of the Yuanjia era waned.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔賑恤郡縣民遭寇者，蠲其稅調。

translations.literal: On guiyou, an edict was issued to relieve and succor the people of the commanderies and counties who had suffered from the invaders, and their taxes and levies were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, an edict ordered relief for the people of ravaged commanderies and counties and remitted their taxes and levies.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，降太尉義恭為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Grand Commandant Yigong was demoted to General of Agile Cavalry with privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Grand Commandant Yigong was demoted to General of Agile Cavalry with privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，魏主濟河。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Wei ruler crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the Wei emperor crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，降鎮軍將軍武陵王駿為北中郎將。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the General of the Pacification Army, the Prince of Wuling, Jun, was demoted to General of the North Center.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Prince Jun of Wuling, General of the Pacification Army, was demoted to General of the North Center.

sentences.zh: 壬午，上如瓜步。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Emperor proceeded to Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the emperor went to Guabu.

sentences.zh: 是日，解嚴。

translations.literal: On that day martial law was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: That same day martial law was lifted.

sentences.zh: 初，魏中書學生盧度世，玄之子也，坐崔浩事亡命匿高陽鄭羆家。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu Dushi, a student of the Wei Secretariat, son of Xuan, because of the Cui Hao affair had fled as a fugitive and hidden himself in the home of Zheng Pi of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lu Dushi, a Wei Secretariat student and son of Lu Xuan, had fled into hiding at the home of Zheng Pi of Gaoyang because of the Cui Hao affair.

sentences.zh: 吏囚羆子，掠治之。

translations.literal: Officials imprisoned Zheng Pi's son and tortured him to extract a confession.
translations.idiomatic: Officials imprisoned Zheng Pi's son and tortured him for information.

sentences.zh: 羆戒其子曰：「君子殺身成仁，雖死不可言。」

translations.literal: Pi admonished his son, saying: "A gentleman gives his life to fulfill humaneness—even in death he does not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Pi warned his son, "A gentleman dies for righteousness—even facing death, he must not speak."

sentences.zh: 其子奉父命，吏以火爇其體，終不言而死。

translations.literal: His son obeyed his father's command; the officials burned his body with fire, and he died without ever speaking.
translations.idiomatic: The son obeyed; officials burned his body with fire, and he died without ever speaking.

sentences.zh: 及魏主臨江，上遣殿上將軍黃延年使於魏，魏主問曰：「盧度世亡命，已應至彼。」

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler came to the river, the Emperor sent the Palace General Huang Yannian as envoy to Wei. The Wei ruler asked: "Lu Dushi fled as a fugitive—he should already have reached your side."
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor reached the Yangtze, the Song emperor sent Palace General Huang Yannian as envoy. The Wei emperor asked, "Lu Dushi fled to your realm—he should have arrived by now."

sentences.zh: 延年曰：「都下不聞有度世也。」

translations.literal: Yannian said: "In the capital we have not heard of Dushi."
translations.idiomatic: Yannian replied, "We have heard nothing of Dushi in the capital."

sentences.zh: 魏主乃赦度世及其族逃亡籍沒者。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler thereupon amnestied Dushi and those of his clan who had fled and whose registers had been confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor then amnestied Dushi and his clan members who had fled and whose property had been confiscated.

sentences.zh: 度世自出，魏主以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Dushi came forth of his own accord, and the Wei ruler appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Dushi surrendered himself, and the Wei emperor appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 度世為其弟娶鄭羆妹以報德。

translations.literal: Dushi had his younger brother marry Zheng Pi's younger sister to repay his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Dushi had his younger brother marry Zheng Pi's sister to repay the family's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙酉，帝還宮。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yiyou, the Emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yiyou, the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏主還平城，飲至告廟，以降民五萬餘家分置近畿。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng, held a victory feast and reported to the ancestral temple, and distributed more than fifty thousand surrendered households among the near metropolitan districts.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng, held a victory feast and reported to the ancestral temple, and resettled more than fifty thousand surrendered households in districts near the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，魏主過彭城，遣人語城中曰：「食盡且去，須麥熟更來。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Wei ruler passed Pengcheng, he sent someone to tell those in the city: "Our food is exhausted and we are leaving for now; when the wheat is ripe we shall come again."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Wei emperor passed Pengcheng, he sent word to the city: "Our provisions are spent and we are leaving for now; when the wheat ripens we shall return."

sentences.zh: 及期，江夏王義恭議欲芟麥翦苗，移民堡聚。

translations.literal: When the appointed time came, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, deliberated on cutting the wheat and trimming the seedlings and moving the people into fortified clusters.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointed time came, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia proposed cutting the wheat, uprooting the seedlings, and relocating the population into fortified settlements.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍錄事參軍王孝孫曰：「虜不能復來，既自可保；

translations.literal: Wang Xiaosun, Recording Secretary of the Pacification Army, said: "The barbarians cannot come again—the crops can be kept as they are;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaosun, Recording Secretary of the Pacification Army, said, "The enemy will not return—the crops can be left alone;

sentences.zh: 如其更至，此議亦不可立。

translations.literal: if they should come again, this plan also could not stand.
translations.idiomatic: and if they do return, this plan would not save us anyway.

sentences.zh: 百姓閉在內城，饑饉日久，方春之月，野采自資；

translations.literal: The common people were shut up in the inner city; famine had lasted a long time, and in the spring month they gathered wild plants to sustain themselves;
translations.idiomatic: The people were confined within the inner city; famine had dragged on, and in spring they foraged in the wild to survive;

sentences.zh: 一入堡聚，餓死立至，民知必死，何可制邪！

translations.literal: once they entered the fortified clusters, death by starvation would come at once—the people knew they would surely die; how could they be restrained!
translations.idiomatic: herd them into fortified clusters and they would starve at once—the people knew it meant certain death; how could you restrain them!

sentences.zh: 虜若必來，芟麥無晚。」

translations.literal: If the barbarians are certain to come, cutting the wheat will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy does come, there will still be time to cut the wheat."

sentences.zh: 四坐默然，莫之敢對。

translations.literal: All present fell silent, and none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly fell silent; no one dared respond.

sentences.zh: 長史張暢曰：「孝孫之議，實有可尋。」

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhang Chang said: "Xiaosun's proposal indeed has points worth considering."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zhang Chang said, "Xiaosun's argument does have merit."

sentences.zh: 鎮軍府典簽董元嗣侍武陵王駿之側，進曰：「王錄事議不可奪。」

translations.literal: Dong Yuansi, Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army headquarters, attending at the side of the Prince of Wuling, Jun, stepped forward and said: "The Recorder's proposal cannot be set aside."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yuansi, chief clerk of the Pacification Army staff, standing beside Prince Jun of Wuling, stepped forward and said, "The Recorder's proposal cannot be overturned."

sentences.zh: 別駕王子夏曰：「此論誠然。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Wang Zixia said: "This argument is indeed so."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Zixia said, "That is certainly true."

sentences.zh: 暢斂板白駿曰：「下官欲命孝孫彈子夏。」

translations.literal: Chang closed his tablet and reported to Jun: "Your subordinate wishes to have Xiaosun rebuke Zixia."
translations.idiomatic: Chang closed his memorial tablet and told Jun, "I intend to have Xiaosun rebuke Zixia."

sentences.zh: 駿曰：「王別駕有何事邪？」

translations.literal: Jun said: "What matter does the Vice Director have?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked, "What has the Vice Director done?"

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「芟麥移民，可謂大議，一方安危，事繫於此。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Cutting the wheat and moving the people may be called a great deliberation—the safety of the region hangs on this.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Cutting the wheat and relocating the population is a weighty matter—the safety of the entire region depends on it.

sentences.zh: 子夏親為州端，曾無同異；

translations.literal: Zixia, as the leading official of the province, had not a word of agreement or dissent;
translations.idiomatic: Zixia, as the province's leading official, offered no opinion either way;

sentences.zh: 及聞元嗣之言，則歡笑酬答。

translations.literal: yet when he heard Yuansi's words, he laughed and responded in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: yet when he heard Yuansi speak, he laughed and chimed in.

sentences.zh: 阿意左右，何以事君！」

translations.literal: To flatter those at one's side—how can one serve one's lord!"
translations.idiomatic: Flattering those around you—how can you serve your prince!"

sentences.zh: 子夏、元嗣皆大慚，義恭之議遂寢。

translations.literal: Zixia and Yuansi were both deeply ashamed, and Yigong's proposal was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Zixia and Yuansi were deeply ashamed, and Yigong's proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初，魯宗之奔魏，其子軌為魏荊州刺史、襄陽公，鎮長社。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lu Zongzhi fled to Wei, his son Gui was made Governor of Jing for Wei and Duke of Xiangyang, stationed at Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Lu Zongzhi defected to Wei, his son Gui became Wei Governor of Jing and Duke of Xiangyang, stationed at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 常思南歸，以昔殺劉康祖及徐湛之之父，故不敢來。

translations.literal: He often thought of returning south, but because he had once killed Liu Kangzu and Xu Zhanzhi's father, he dared not come.
translations.idiomatic: He longed to return south, but having once killed Liu Kangzu and Xu Zhanzhi's father, he dared not defect.

sentences.zh: 軌卒，子爽襲父官爵。

translations.literal: When Gui died, his son Shuang inherited his father's office and title.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui died, his son Shuang inherited his father's post and title.

sentences.zh: 爽少有武干，與弟秀皆有寵於魏主，秀為中書郎。

translations.literal: Shuang in his youth had martial ability; he and his younger brother Xiu were both favored by the Wei ruler, and Xiu was a Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang showed martial talent from youth; he and his younger brother Xiu both enjoyed the Wei emperor's favor, and Xiu served as a Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 既而兄弟各有罪，魏主詰責之。

translations.literal: Before long the brothers each had offenses, and the Wei ruler rebuked and blamed them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both brothers fell under suspicion, and the Wei emperor rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 爽、秀懼誅，從魏主自瓜步還，至湖陸，請曰：「奴與南有仇，每兵來，常恐禍及墳墓。

translations.literal: Shuang and Xiu, fearing execution, as they followed the Wei ruler back from Guabu to Huliu, requested: "Your servants have enemies in the south; whenever troops come, we always fear harm to our ancestral graves.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing execution, Shuang and Xiu, accompanying the Wei emperor back from Guabu, petitioned at Huliu: "We have enemies in the south; whenever armies march south, we fear for our ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 乞共迎喪還葬平城。」

translations.literal: We beg to go together to bring back the coffins and bury them at Pingcheng."
translations.idiomatic: We beg leave to retrieve our ancestors' remains and bury them at Pingcheng."

sentences.zh: 魏主許之，爽至長社，殺魏戍兵數百人，帥部曲及願從者千餘家奔汝南。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler granted it. When Shuang reached Changshe, he killed several hundred Wei garrison troops and led his retainers and more than a thousand households who wished to follow him in flight to Runan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor consented. At Changshe, Shuang killed several hundred Wei garrison troops and led his retainers and more than a thousand willing households in flight to Runan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，爽遣秀詣壽陽，奉書於南平王鑠以請降。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Shuang sent Xiu to Shouyang to present a letter to the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Shuang sent Xiu to Shouyang with a letter to Prince Shuo of Nanping offering surrender.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，大喜，以爽為司州刺史，鎮義陽；

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he was greatly pleased and appointed Shuang Governor of Si, stationed at Yiyang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and appointed Shuang Governor of Si, stationed at Yiyang;

sentences.zh: 秀為穎川太守，餘弟侄並授官爵，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Xiu was made Administrator of Yingchuan; the remaining younger brothers and nephews were all granted offices and titles, with very generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu became Administrator of Yingchuan; the remaining brothers and nephews received offices and titles, with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 魏人毀其墳墓。

translations.literal: The Wei destroyed their ancestral graves.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei destroyed their family graves.

sentences.zh: 徐湛之以為廟算遠圖，特所獎納，不敢苟申私怨，乞屏居田裡；

translations.literal: Xu Zhanzhi, holding that this was a long-range plan of the temple altars and specially to be rewarded, dared not lightly press a private grievance and requested to withdraw and live in the countryside;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhanzhi, recognizing this as a far-sighted strategic gain, dared not press a personal vendetta and asked to retire to his estates;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 青州民司馬順則自稱晉室近屬，聚眾號齊王。

translations.literal: A man of Qing province, Sima Shunze, declared himself a near kinsman of the Jin house, gathered a crowd, and styled himself King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Qing province, Sima Shunze claimed descent from the Jin imperial house, raised a following, and proclaimed himself King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 梁鄒戍主崔勳之詣州，五月，乙酉，順則乘虛襲據梁鄒城。

translations.literal: Cui Xunzhi, commander of the Liangzou garrison, went to the provincial capital; in the fifth month, on yiyou, Shunze seized the opportunity and raided and occupied Liangzou city.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xunzhi, garrison commander at Liangzou, had gone to the provincial capital; in the fifth month, on yiyou, Shunze seized the moment and captured Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 又有沙門自稱司馬百年，亦聚眾號安定王以應之。

translations.literal: There was also a monk who called himself Sima Bainian, who likewise gathered a crowd and styled himself King of Anding to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: A monk also called himself Sima Bainian, raised followers, and proclaimed himself King of Anding in support.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On renyin, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以江夏王義恭領南兗州刺史，徙鎮盱眙。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, was made concurrent Governor of Southern Yan and transferred to garrison Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was appointed concurrent Governor of Southern Yan and transferred his headquarters to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 增督十二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: His supervision of military affairs in twelve provinces was increased.
translations.idiomatic: His authority over military affairs in twelve provinces was expanded.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以尚書左僕射何尚之為尚書令，太子詹事徐湛之為僕射、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: On wushen, He Shangzhi, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat, and Xu Zhanzhi, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Vice Director and General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, He Shangzhi, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, became Director of the Secretariat, and Xu Zhanzhi, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, became Vice Director and General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 尚之以湛之國戚，任遇隆重，每事推之。

translations.literal: Shangzhi, because Zhanzhi was a kinsman by marriage, treated him with heavy favor and deferred to him in every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhanzhi was a royal in-law, Shangzhi treated him with exceptional favor and deferred to him on every matter.

sentences.zh: 詔湛之與尚之並受辭訴。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Zhanzhi and Shangzhi should both receive petitions and complaints.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that Zhanzhi and Shangzhi should both receive petitions and appeals.

sentences.zh: 尚之雖為令，而朝事悉歸湛之。

translations.literal: Although Shangzhi was Director, court affairs all fell to Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shangzhi held the title of Director, court affairs all passed through Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬戌，魏改元正平。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renxu, Wei changed the era name to Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renxu, Wei changed the era name to Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 魏主命太子少傅游雅、中書侍郎胡方回等更定律令，多所增損，凡三百九十一條。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler ordered the Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, You Ya, the Secretariat Gentleman Hu Fanghui, and others to revise the laws and ordinances, with many additions and deletions—three hundred ninety-one articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered Junior Tutor You Ya, Secretariat Gentleman Hu Fanghui, and others to revise the legal code, with extensive additions and deletions—three hundred ninety-one articles in all.

sentences.zh: 魏太子晃監國，頗信任左右，又營園田，收其利。

translations.literal: The Wei Heir Apparent Huang supervised the state, trusted his close attendants considerably, and also developed garden estates, collecting their profits.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Crown Prince Huang supervised the realm, placed great trust in his close attendants, and developed private estates to profit from them.

sentences.zh: 高允諫曰：「天地無私，故能覆載，王者無私，故能容養。

translations.literal: Gao Yun remonstrated, saying: "Heaven and earth are without partiality, and therefore can cover and bear up all things; a king is without partiality, and therefore can nourish and sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun remonstrated: "Heaven and earth are impartial, and therefore sustain all things; a ruler is impartial, and therefore nurtures all his people.

sentences.zh: 今殿下國之儲貳，萬方所則，而營立私田，畜養雞犬，乃至酤販市廛，與民爭利；

translations.literal: Now Your Highness is the state's heir designate, the model for all directions, yet you establish private fields, raise chickens and dogs, and even sell goods in the market stalls, competing with the people for profit;
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is the heir to the realm, the model for all the world, yet you establish private estates, raise livestock, and even sell goods in the markets, competing with the common people for profit;

sentences.zh: 謗聲流布，不可追掩。

translations.literal: slander spreads abroad and cannot be overtaken and covered up.
translations.idiomatic: slander spreads and cannot be recalled.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，殿下之天下，富有四海，何求而無，乃與販夫販婦競此尺寸之利乎！

translations.literal: The realm is Your Highness's realm—you possess the four seas; what could you seek and not obtain? Yet you compete with peddlers male and female for these trifling profits!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is yours—you possess all within the four seas; what could you lack? Yet you compete with street peddlers for petty profits!

sentences.zh: 昔虢之將亡，神賜之土田，漢靈帝私立府藏，皆有顛覆之禍；

translations.literal: In former times, when Guo was about to perish, the spirits bestowed land upon it; Emperor Ling of Han established a private treasury—both met with the calamity of overthrow;
translations.idiomatic: When Guo was about to fall, the spirits granted it land; Emperor Ling of Han established a private treasury—both brought ruin upon themselves;

sentences.zh: 前鑒若此，甚可畏也。

translations.literal: precedents such as these are greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: such precedents are deeply alarming.

sentences.zh: 武王愛國、邵、齊、華，所以王天下；

translations.literal: King Wu cherished Guo, Shao, Qi, and Hua, and thereby became king over the realm;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu cherished worthy ministers and thereby ruled the realm;

sentences.zh: 殷紂受飛廉、惡來，所以喪其國。

translations.literal: King Zhou of Yin accepted Feilian and Elai, and thereby lost his state.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Yin embraced Feilian and Elai, and thereby lost his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 今東宮俊乂不少，頃來侍御左右者，恐非在朝之選。

translations.literal: Now the Eastern Palace has no lack of talented men; those who have recently attended at your side, I fear, are not choices fit for the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace has no shortage of talent; those who have lately attended you, I fear, are not men fit for court.

sentences.zh: 願殿下斥去佞邪，親近忠良，所在田園，分給貧下，販賣之物，以時收散；

translations.literal: I wish that Your Highness would drive away flatterers and the wicked, draw near to the loyal and good, distribute the garden estates to the poor, and gather up and disperse the goods for sale in due season;
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Highness to dismiss flatterers and the wicked, draw near to the loyal and good, distribute your estates to the poor, and wind down your commercial ventures in good time;

sentences.zh: 如此，則休聲日至，謗議可除矣。」

translations.literal: if this is done, then good reputation will increase day by day, and slander can be removed."
translations.idiomatic: then your reputation will grow daily and slander will cease."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The prince did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 太子為政精察，而中常侍宗愛，性險暴，多不法，太子惡之。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent in governing was precise and searching, but the Palace Attendant Zong Ai was by nature dangerous and violent, with many unlawful acts, and the Heir Apparent detested him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince governed with sharp scrutiny, but Palace Attendant Zong Ai was violent and lawless by nature, and the prince detested him.

sentences.zh: 給事中仇尼道盛、侍郎任平城有寵於太子，頗用事，皆與愛不協。

translations.literal: Qiu Ni Daosheng, Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, and Ren Pingcheng, Gentleman of the Palace, were favored by the Heir Apparent and wielded considerable power; both were at odds with Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Ni Daosheng, Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, and Ren Pingcheng, Gentleman of the Palace, enjoyed the crown prince's favor and wielded considerable influence; both were at odds with Ai.

sentences.zh: 愛恐為道盛等所糾，遂構告其罪，魏主怒，斬道盛等於都街，東宮官屬多坐死，帝怒甚。

translations.literal: Ai feared being impeached by Daosheng and the others, and therefore fabricated charges against them. The Wei ruler was enraged and executed Daosheng and the others in the capital streets; many officials of the Eastern Palace were condemned to death, and the Emperor's anger was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Ai feared impeachment by Daosheng and his allies, fabricated charges, and the Wei emperor, enraged, executed them in the capital streets; many Eastern Palace officials were put to death, and the emperor's fury was extreme.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，太子以憂卒。

translations.literal: On wuchen, the Heir Apparent died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the crown prince died of grief.

sentences.zh: 壬申，葬金陵，謚曰景穆。

translations.literal: On renshen, he was buried at Jinling, with the posthumous title Jingmu.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, he was buried at Jinling with the posthumous title Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 帝徐知太子無罪，甚悔之。

translations.literal: The Emperor gradually came to know that the Heir Apparent was without guilt and deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually the emperor realized the crown prince was innocent and deeply regretted his actions.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁亥，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai, the Wei ruler went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai, the Wei emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 青、冀二州刺史蕭斌遣振武將軍劉武之等擊司馬順則、司馬百年，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin, Governor of Qing and Ji, sent the General Who Exalts Martial Virtue, Liu Wuzhi, and others to attack Sima Shunze and Sima Bainian; both were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin, Governor of Qing and Ji, sent General Liu Wuzhi and others against Sima Shunze and Sima Bainian; both were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，梁鄒平。

translations.literal: On guihai, Liangzou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Liangzou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌、王玄謨皆坐退敗免官。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo were both stripped of office on account of retreat and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo were both dismissed for retreating in defeat.

sentences.zh: 上問沈慶之曰：「斌欲斬玄謨而卿止之，何也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Shen Qingzhi: "Bin wished to behead Xuemo, but you stopped him—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Shen Qingzhi, "Bin wanted to execute Xuemo, but you stopped him—why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「諸將奔退，莫不懼罪；

translations.literal: He replied: "The generals in flight and retreat all feared punishment;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Every retreating general feared punishment;

sentences.zh: 自歸而死，將至逃散，故止之。」

translations.literal: if those who returned of their own accord were put to death, the generals would flee and scatter—therefore I stopped it."
translations.idiomatic: execute men who surrendered willingly and the rest would scatter in flight—that is why I stopped it."

sentences.zh: 九月，癸巳，魏主還平城；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guisi, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guisi, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng;

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚申，復如陰山。

translations.literal: in winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, he again went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: in winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, he went to Yinshan again.

sentences.zh: 上遣使至魏，魏遣殿中將軍郎法祐來修好。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent an envoy to Wei, and Wei sent the Palace General Lang Fayou to come and restore friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor sent an envoy to Wei, and Wei sent Palace General Lang Fayou to restore friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 己巳，魏上黨靖王長孫道生卒。

translations.literal: On jisi, Changsun Daosheng, Prince Jing of Shangdang for Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Changsun Daosheng, Prince Jing of Shangdang, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁丑，魏主封景穆太子之子濬為高陽王；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingchou, the Wei ruler enfeoffed Jun, son of the Jingmu Heir Apparent, as Prince of Gaoyang;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingchou, the Wei emperor enfeoffed Jun, son of Crown Prince Jingmu, as Prince of Gaoyang;

sentences.zh: 既而以皇孫世嫡，不當為籓王，乃止。

translations.literal: but then, because as the legitimate heir of the imperial grandson he ought not to be made a feudal prince, it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: but because he was the legitimate imperial grandson, he should not hold a feudal title, and the enfeoffment was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 時濬生四年，聰達過人，魏主愛之，常置左右。

translations.literal: At the time Jun was four years old, clever and penetrating beyond others; the Wei ruler loved him and constantly kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was then four years old, precocious beyond his years; the Wei emperor adored him and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 徙秦王翰為東平王，燕王譚為臨淮王，楚王建為廣陽王，吳王余為南安王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Han, was transferred to Prince of Dongping; the Prince of Yan, Tan, to Prince of Linhuai; the Prince of Chu, Jian, to Prince of Guangyang; and the Prince of Wu, Yu, to Prince of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Han of Qin became Prince of Dongping; Prince Tan of Yan became Prince of Linhuai; Prince Jian of Chu became Prince of Guangyang; and Prince Yu of Wu became Prince of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 帝使沈慶之徙彭城流民數千家於瓜步，征北參軍程天祚徙江西流民數千家於姑孰。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Shen Qingzhi relocate several thousand refugee households from Pengcheng to Guabu, and Cheng Tianzuo, Staff Officer of the Northern Campaign, relocate several thousand refugee households from west of the river to Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Shen Qingzhi resettle several thousand refugee families from Pengcheng at Guabu, and Cheng Tianzuo, staff officer of the northern campaign, resettle several thousand refugee families from west of the Yangtze at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 帝以吏部郎王僧綽為侍中。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Wang Sengchuo, Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Wang Sengchuo, Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 僧綽，曇首之子也，幼有大成之度，眾皆以國器許之。

translations.literal: Sengchuo was the son of Tan Shou; from youth he had the measure of great accomplishment, and all regarded him as material for the state's vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo was the son of Tan Shou; from childhood he showed the makings of greatness, and all regarded him as destined for high office.

sentences.zh: 好學，有思理，練悉朝典。

translations.literal: He loved learning, had powers of reflection and reason, and was thoroughly versed in court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, thought deeply, and was thoroughly versed in court protocol.

sentences.zh: 尚帝女東陽獻公主。

translations.literal: He married the Emperor's daughter, the Xian Princess of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He married the emperor's daughter, the Xian Princess of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 在吏部，諳悉人物，舉拔鹹得其分。

translations.literal: While in the Ministry of Personnel, he was thoroughly acquainted with men and affairs, and in promotions and selections all were placed according to their proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ministry of Personnel, he knew every candidate intimately and placed each appointment exactly where it belonged.

sentences.zh: 及為侍中，年二十九，沉深有局度，不以才能高人。

translations.literal: When he became Palace Attendant, he was twenty-nine years old, deep and steady with a sense of measure, and did not set himself above others by his talent.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Palace Attendant at twenty-nine, he was grave and measured, never condescending to others on account of his talent.

sentences.zh: 帝頗以後事為念，以其年少，欲大相付託，朝政小大，皆與參焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor was much concerned about affairs after his time; because Sengchuo was young, he wished to entrust great matters to him, and in court affairs great and small he was all consulted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful of the succession, wished to entrust him with weighty matters despite his youth, and consulted him on affairs great and small.

sentences.zh: 帝之始親政事也，委任王華、王曇首、殷景仁、謝弘微、劉湛，次則范曄、沈演之、庾炳之，最後江湛、徐湛之、何瑀之及僧綽，凡十二人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first personally attended to government affairs, he entrusted Wang Hua, Wang Tan Shou, Yin Jingren, Xie Hongwei, and Liu Zhan; next Fan Ye, Shen Yanzhi, and Yu Bingzhi; and finally Jiang Zhan, Xu Zhanzhi, He Yuzhi, and Sengchuo—twelve men in all.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took personal charge of government, he relied on Wang Hua, Wang Tan Shou, Yin Jingren, Xie Hongwei, and Liu Zhan; then Fan Ye, Shen Yanzhi, and Yu Bingzhi; and finally Jiang Zhan, Xu Zhanzhi, He Yuzhi, and Sengchuo—twelve men in all.

sentences.zh: 康和入朝於魏，魏主厚禮之。

translations.literal: Kang He entered court audience in Wei, and the Wei ruler treated him with generous ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Kang He paid court to Wei, and the Wei emperor received him with lavish honors.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝下之上元嘉二十九年（

translations.literal: Upper portion of the Annals of Taizu the Literary Emperor, Yuanjia year twenty-nine (
translations.idiomatic: From the upper section of the reign of Emperor Wen, the Literary Emperor—Yuanjia, year twenty-nine (

sentences.zh: 壬辰，公元四五二年）

translations.literal: renchen, CE 452)
translations.idiomatic: renchen, 452 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，魏所得宋民五千餘家在中山者謀叛，州軍討誅之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, more than five thousand Song households taken by Wei and settled at Zhongshan plotted rebellion, and the provincial army pursued and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, more than five thousand Song captives settled at Zhongshan plotted rebellion, and provincial troops suppressed and executed them.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史張掖王沮渠萬年坐與叛者通謀。

translations.literal: Juqu Wannian, Prince of Zhangye and Governor of Ji, was implicated for communicating and plotting with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Wannian, Prince of Zhangye and Governor of Ji, was implicated for conspiring with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賜死。

translations.literal: He was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 魏世祖追悼景穆太子不已，中常侍宗愛懼誅，二月，甲寅，弒帝，尚書左僕射蘭延、侍中和疋、薛提等秘不發喪。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor Wudi ceaselessly mourned the Jingmu Heir Apparent. The Palace Attendant Zong Ai, fearing execution, in the second month, on jiayin, assassinated the Emperor. Lan Yan, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, He Pi, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Xue Ti, and others secretly did not announce the death.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Wudi mourned Crown Prince Jingmu without cease. Palace Attendant Zong Ai, fearing execution, assassinated the emperor in the second month, on jiayin. Lan Yan, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, He Pi, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Xue Ti, and others concealed the death.

sentences.zh: 延、疋以皇孫濬沖幼，欲立長君，征秦王翰，置之秘室；

translations.literal: Yan and Pi, because the imperial grandson Jun was young and tender, wished to establish an elder ruler and placed the Prince of Qin, Han, in a secret chamber;
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Pi, considering the young age of imperial grandson Jun, wished to install an elder ruler and confined Prince Han of Qin in a secret chamber;

sentences.zh: 提以濬嫡皇孫，不可廢。

translations.literal: Ti held that Jun, as the legitimate imperial grandson, could not be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Ti argued that Jun, as the legitimate imperial grandson, could not be passed over.

sentences.zh: 議久不決。

translations.literal: Deliberation went on long without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 宗愛知之，自以得罪於景穆太子，而素惡秦王翰，善南安王余，乃密迎余自中宮便門入禁中，矯稱赫連皇后令召延等。

translations.literal: Ai learned of it. He considered that he had given offense to the Jingmu Heir Apparent, had long detested the Prince of Qin, Han, and was on good terms with the Prince of Nan'an, Yu; he therefore secretly welcomed Yu through the side gate of the inner palace into the forbidden precincts and forged an order in the name of Empress Helian to summon Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Ai learned of the dispute. Believing he had offended Crown Prince Jingmu, having long hated Prince Han of Qin while favoring Prince Yu of Nan'an, he secretly brought Yu through the inner palace side gate and forged an summons in Empress Helian's name to call Yan and the others.

sentences.zh: 延等以愛素賤，不以為疑，皆隨入。

translations.literal: Yan and the others, because Ai had always been base, did not suspect him and all followed in.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the others, deeming Ai too lowly to be dangerous, suspected nothing and all entered.

sentences.zh: 愛先使宦者三十人持兵伏於禁中，延等入，以次收縛，斬之；

translations.literal: Ai had first sent thirty eunuchs bearing arms to lie in ambush within the forbidden precincts. When Yan and the others entered, they were seized and bound in turn and beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: Ai had stationed thirty armed eunuchs in ambush within the palace. As Yan and the others entered, they were seized one by one and beheaded;

sentences.zh: 殺秦王翰於永巷而立余。

translations.literal: killed the Prince of Qin, Han, in the Eternal Lane, and established Yu.
translations.idiomatic: killed Prince Han of Qin in the Eternal Lane and installed Yu as emperor.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元承平，尊皇后為皇太后，以愛為大司馬、大將軍、太師、都督中外諸軍事、領中秘書，封馮翊王。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name was changed to Chengping, the Empress was honored as Empress Dowager, and Ai was made Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, and Concurrent Director of the Central Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name changed to Chengping, the empress was elevated to empress dowager, and Ai was appointed Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, and Concurrent Director of the Central Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 庚午，立皇子休仁為建安王。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the imperial son Xiuren was established as Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Prince Xiuren was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛卯，魏葬太武皇帝於金陵，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinmao, Wei buried the Emperor Taiwu at Jinling; his temple title was Emperor Wudi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinmao, Wei interred Emperor Taiwu at Jinling, with the temple title Emperor Wudi.

sentences.zh: 上聞魏世祖殂，更謀北伐，魯爽等復勸之。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing that Wei Emperor Wudi had died, again plotted a northern campaign; Lu Shuang and others again urged it.
translations.idiomatic: On word that Wei Emperor Wudi was dead, the emperor again planned a northern expedition, and Lu Shuang and others pressed him once more.

sentences.zh: 上訪於群臣，太子中庶子何偃以為：「淮、泗數州瘡痍未復，不宜輕動。」

translations.literal: The emperor consulted the ministers. He Yan, Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent, held: "The several prefectures of Huai and Si have wounds not yet healed—it is not fitting to move lightly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sought counsel from his ministers. He Yan, Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent, argued: "The Huai and Si region remains devastated; we ought not stir lightly."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 偃，尚之之子也。

translations.literal: Yan was the son of He Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was a son of He Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，丙申，詔曰：「虐虜窮凶，著於自昔；

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on bingshen, an edict said: "The cruel barbarians' extreme villainy has been manifest from of old;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on bingshen, an edict proclaimed: "These savage foes have been implacably wicked since time out of mind;

sentences.zh: 未勞資斧，已伏天誅。

translations.literal: before we had to raise the executioner's axe, they have already submitted to Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: ere we lifted a single axe, Heaven has already struck them down.

sentences.zh: 拯溺蕩穢，今其會也。

translations.literal: To rescue the drowning and sweep away filth—now is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: To rescue the drowning and scour away corruption—this is the hour.

sentences.zh: 可符驃騎、司空二府，各部分所統，東西應接。

translations.literal: Let orders be sent to the two offices of the Cavalry General-in-Chief and the Minister of Works, each dividing what they command, east and west linking in support.
translations.idiomatic: Notify the offices of the Cavalry General-in-Chief and the Minister of Works to divide their commands and link east and west in concert.

sentences.zh: 歸義建績者，隨勞酬獎。」

translations.literal: Those who return in allegiance and establish merit shall receive rewards according to their labor."
translations.idiomatic: All who submit and distinguish themselves shall be rewarded according to their service."

sentences.zh: 於是遣撫軍將軍蕭思話督冀州刺史張永等向碻磝，魯爽、魯秀、程天祚將荊州甲士四萬出許、洛，雍州刺史臧質帥所領趣潼關。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched the General Who Pacifies the Army, Xiao Sihua, to oversee Jizhou Inspector Zhang Yong and others toward Que'ao; Lu Shuang, Lu Xiu, and Cheng Tianzuo led forty thousand armored troops of Jingzhou out through Xu and Luo; Yongzhou Inspector Zang Zhi led his force toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent General Who Pacifies the Army Xiao Sihua to command Jizhou Inspector Zhang Yong and others against Que'ao; Lu Shuang, Lu Xiu, and Cheng Tianzuo advanced forty thousand Jingzhou armored troops through Xu and Luoyang; Yongzhou Inspector Zang Zhi marched his command toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 永，茂度之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong was the son of Zhang Maodu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong was a son of Zhang Maodu.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之固諫北伐；

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi firmly remonstrated against the northern campaign;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi argued fiercely against the northern expedition;

sentences.zh: 上以其異議，不使行。

translations.literal: the emperor, because of his dissenting view, did not let him go.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor barred him from the campaign for his dissent.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史劉興祖上言，以為：「河南阻饑，野無所掠；

translations.literal: Liu Xingzu, Governor of Qingzhou, submitted a memorial, holding: "Henan is blocked by famine; in the wilds there is nothing to plunder;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingzu, Governor of Qingzhou, memorialized: "Henan suffers famine; the countryside offers nothing to forage;

sentences.zh: 脫諸城固守，非旬月可拔。

translations.literal: if the cities all hold firm, they cannot be taken in less than a ten-day month.
translations.idiomatic: if enemy towns stand fast, none will fall within weeks.

sentences.zh: 稽留大眾，轉輸方勞；

translations.literal: to detain the great host, transport supplies will only grow toilsome;
translations.idiomatic: Holding a vast army idle will only exhaust our supply lines;

sentences.zh: 應機乘勢，事存急速。

translations.literal: seizing the moment according to circumstance—the matter rests on speed.
translations.idiomatic: we must seize the moment—speed is everything.

sentences.zh: 今偽帥始死，兼逼暑時，國內猜擾，不暇遠赴。

translations.literal: Now the false ruler has just died; moreover it presses toward hot season; within the state suspicion and turmoil—there is no leisure to come from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Their puppet lord is newly dead; summer heat presses upon them; their realm seethes with suspicion—they cannot look far afield.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜長驅中山，據其關要。

translations.literal: In my humble view, one should drive straight for Zhongshan and seize its strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: I urge a long thrust to Zhongshan to seize its strategic choke points.

sentences.zh: 冀州以北，民人尚豐，兼麥已向熟，因資為易，向義之徒，必應響赴。

translations.literal: North of Jizhou the people are still plentiful, and the wheat moreover is turning ripe—drawing on supplies will be easy; those inclined to righteousness will surely answer and flock in.
translations.idiomatic: North of Jizhou the people remain numerous and the wheat is ripening—logistics would be easy, and those yearning for our cause would rally to us.

sentences.zh: 若中州震動，黃河以南，自當消潰。

translations.literal: If the central provinces are shaken, south of the Yellow River will of itself dissolve and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heartland convulses, everything south of the Yellow River will crumble of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 臣請發青、冀七千兵，遣將領之，直入其心腹。

translations.literal: Your subject requests to raise seven thousand troops of Qing and Ji, send a general to lead them, and drive straight into their heartland.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to raise seven thousand men from Qing and Ji, place them under a commander, and strike deep into the enemy's vitals.

sentences.zh: 若前驅克勝，張永及河南眾軍宜一時濟河，使聲實兼舉，並建司牧，撫柔初附，西拒太行，北塞軍都，因事指麾，隨宜加授，畏威欣寵，人百其懷。

translations.literal: If the vanguard wins and prevails, Zhang Yong and the hosts of Henan should cross the river at once, so that reputation and substance rise together; simultaneously establish inspectors and governors, soothe and mollify the newly submitted, block westward at the Taihang, seal northward at Jundu; as affairs dictate give orders, add grants as fitting—those awed by might and delighted at favor, each will have his own heart's wish.
translations.idiomatic: If the vanguard prevails, Zhang Yong and the Henan armies should cross the river at once, so that show of force and real power advance together; establish regional governors to win over fresh converts, hold the Taihang to the west and Jundu Pass to the north; reward and appoint as events warrant—men will fear our might and welcome our grace, each in his own way.

sentences.zh: 若能成功，清壹可待；

translations.literal: If we can succeed, unity and clarity may await;
translations.idiomatic: Success would bring reunification within reach;

sentences.zh: 若不克捷，不為大傷。

translations.literal: if we do not gain victory, it will not be a great harm.
translations.idiomatic: even failure would cost us little.

sentences.zh: 並催促裝束，伏聽敕旨。」

translations.literal: All are urged to hasten preparations; we bow and await your command."
translations.idiomatic: All stands ready—awaiting your orders."

sentences.zh: 上意止存河南，亦不從。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent was only to hold Henan, and he again did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor's aim was only to secure Henan, and he again refused.

sentences.zh: 上又使員外散騎侍郎琅邪徐爰隨軍向碻磝，銜中旨授諸將方略，臨時宣示。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent Xu Ai of Langye, Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, with the army toward Que'ao, bearing the central intent to confer strategy on the generals, announcing it on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Xu Ai of Langye, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, with the army to Que'ao to convey imperial strategy to the commanders as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 尚書令何尚之以老請致仕，退居方山。

translations.literal: He Shangzhi, Director of the Secretariat, by reason of age requested to retire from office and withdrew to reside at Mount Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi, Director of the Secretariat, pleaded old age and retired to Mount Fang.

sentences.zh: 議者鹹謂尚之不能固志。

translations.literal: Discussants all said Shangzhi could not firm his will.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Shangzhi lacked the resolve to hold to his purpose.

sentences.zh: 既而詔書敦諭數四，六月，戊申朔，尚之復起視事。

translations.literal: Before long edicts earnestly admonished him repeatedly; in the sixth month, on the first day of wushen, Shangzhi again rose and attended to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts repeatedly urged him back; in the sixth month, on the first day of wushen, Shangzhi returned to office.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞袁涉錄自古隱士有跡無名者為《真隱傳》以嗤之。

translations.literal: Yuan She, Imperial Censor, compiled from antiquity recluses who left traces but no names into True Recluses to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan She, Imperial Censor, compiled True Recluses—a roster of ancient hermits who left traces but no names—to lampoon him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，張永等至碻磝，引兵圍之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Yong and others reached Que'ao and led troops to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Yong and his forces reached Que'ao and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，徙汝陽王渾為武昌王，淮陽王彧為湘東王。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Prince of Ruyang, Hun, was moved to be Prince of Wuchang; the Prince of Huaiyang, Yu, was made Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Prince Hun of Ruyang was reassigned as Prince of Wuchang, and Prince Yu of Huaiyang as Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 初，潘淑妃生始興王濬。

translations.literal: Earlier, Consort Pan Shufei bore Prince Jun of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Consort Pan Shufei had borne Prince Jun of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 元皇后性妒，以淑妃有寵於上，恚恨而殂，淑妃專總內政。

translations.literal: The Primary Empress was jealous by nature; because the consort had favor with the emperor, she died in resentment and rage; the consort alone oversaw inner administration.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was jealous; seeing Consort Pan favored by the emperor, she died embittered, and Consort Pan came to dominate the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 由是太子劭深惡淑妃及濬。

translations.literal: Thereby Crown Prince Shao deeply hated the consort and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shao therefore hated Consort Pan and Jun bitterly.

sentences.zh: 濬懼為將來之禍，乃曲意事劭，劭更與之善。

translations.literal: Jun feared becoming a future calamity and therefore bent his will to serve Shao; Shao became even more friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, fearing for his future, ingratiated himself with Shao, and Shao grew warmer toward him.

sentences.zh: 吳興巫嚴道育，自言能辟谷服食，役使鬼物；

translations.literal: The witch Yan Daoyu of Wuxing claimed she could abstain from grain and take elixirs, and command ghosts and spirits;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Daoyu, a witch of Wuxing, claimed she could live without grain, ingest elixirs, and command spirits;

sentences.zh: 因東陽公主婢王鸚鵡出入主家。

translations.literal: through the Princess of Dongyang's maid Wang Yingwu she came and went in the princess's household.
translations.idiomatic: she gained access to the Princess of Dongyang's household through the princess's maid, Wang Yingwu.

sentences.zh: 道育謂主曰：「神將有符賜主。」

translations.literal: Daoyu said to the princess: "The spirits will have tokens to bestow on Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu told the princess, "The spirits will grant you a sign."

sentences.zh: 主夜臥，見流光若螢，飛入書笥，開視，得二青珠；

translations.literal: At night the princess lay down and saw flowing light like fireflies fly into her document case; opening it to look, she obtained two blue-green pearls;
translations.idiomatic: One night as the princess slept, she saw a glimmer like fireflies fly into her document case; when she opened it, she found two green pearls;

sentences.zh: 由是主與劭、濬皆信惑之。

translations.literal: thereby the princess and Shao and Jun all believed and were deluded by her.
translations.idiomatic: after that the princess, Shao, and Jun all believed in her.

sentences.zh: 劭、濬並多過失，數為上所詰責；

translations.literal: Shao and Jun both had many faults and repeatedly were interrogated and reproached by the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Shao and Jun had many faults and were often rebuked by the emperor;

sentences.zh: 使道育訴請，欲令過不上聞。

translations.literal: they had Daoyu petition and plead, wishing their faults would not reach the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: they had Daoyu intercede with heaven so their faults would never reach the emperor.

sentences.zh: 道育曰：「我已為上天陳請，必不洩露。」

translations.literal: Daoyu said: "I have already laid the matter before Heaven in petition; it will surely not be disclosed."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu said, "I have already petitioned heaven on your behalf; nothing will be disclosed."

sentences.zh: 劭等敬事之，號曰：「天師」。

translations.literal: Shao and the others revered and served her, calling her "Celestial Master."
translations.idiomatic: Shao and the others revered her and called her "the Celestial Master."

sentences.zh: 其後遂與道育、鸚鵡及東陽主奴陳天與、黃門陳慶國共為巫蠱，琢玉為上形像，埋於含章殿前；

translations.literal: Afterward they thereupon with Daoyu, Yingwu, and the Princess of Dongyang's slave Chen Tianyu and Palace Attendant Chen Qingguo together practiced witchcraft and sorcery, carved jade into the emperor's form, and buried it before Hall of Inclusion of Glory;
translations.idiomatic: Later they joined Daoyu, Yingwu, the Princess of Dongyang's slave Chen Tianyu, and palace attendant Chen Qingguo in witchcraft, carving a jade image of the emperor and burying it before the Hall of Inclusion of Glory;

sentences.zh: 劭補天與為隊主。

translations.literal: Shao appointed Tianyu as company chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shao appointed Tianyu company chief.

sentences.zh: 東陽主卒，鸚鵡應出嫁，劭、濬慮語洩，濬府佐吳興沈懷遠；

translations.literal: The Princess of Dongyang died; Yingwu was due to marry out; Shao and Jun feared words would leak; Jun's staff member Shen Huaiyuan of Wuxing—
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess of Dongyang died, Yingwu was due to marry out; Shao and Jun feared she would talk; Jun's staff member Shen Huaiyuan of Wuxing—

sentences.zh: 素為濬所厚，以鸚鵡嫁之為妾。

translations.literal: whom Jun had long favored—was given Yingwu in marriage as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: whom Jun had long favored—received Yingwu as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 上聞天與領隊，以讓劭曰：「汝所用隊主副，並是奴邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor heard Tianyu led a company and reproached Shao, saying: "The company chiefs and deputies you employ—are they all slaves?"
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Tianyu led a company, the emperor reproached Shao: "Are all your company chiefs and deputies slaves?"

sentences.zh: 劭懼，以書告濬。

translations.literal: Shao was afraid and informed Jun by letter.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, alarmed, wrote to Jun.

sentences.zh: 濬復書曰：「彼人若所為不已，正可促其餘命，或是大慶之漸耳。」

translations.literal: Jun wrote back: "If that man does not cease such conduct, one may just hasten the remainder of his life—or perhaps it is the first step toward great rejoicing."
translations.idiomatic: Jun wrote back: "If that man will not stop, we may as well shorten what life he has left—or perhaps this is the dawn of our great deliverance."

sentences.zh: 劭、濬相與往來書疏，常謂上為「彼人」，或曰：「其人」，謂江夏王義恭為「佞人」。

translations.literal: Shao and Jun in mutual correspondence often called the emperor "that man," or said "the man," and called Prince Yigong of Jiangxia "the flatterer."
translations.idiomatic: In their letters Shao and Jun routinely called the emperor "that man" or "the man," and Prince Yigong of Jiangxia "the toady."

sentences.zh: 鸚鵡先與天與私通，既適懷遠，恐事洩，白劭使密殺之。

translations.literal: Yingwu had earlier had private relations with Tianyu; having been given to Huaiyuan, she feared the matter would leak and told Shao to have him secretly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yingwu had earlier slept with Tianyu; now married to Huaiyuan, she feared exposure and urged Shao to have Tianyu killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 陳慶國懼，曰：「巫蠱事，唯我與天與宣傳往來。

translations.literal: Chen Qingguo was afraid and said: "In the witchcraft affair, only Tianyu and I carried word back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingguo panicked and said, "In the witchcraft plot, only Tianyu and I carried messages.

sentences.zh: 今天與死，我其危哉！」

translations.literal: Now Tianyu is dead—I am surely in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Tianyu is dead—I am doomed!"

sentences.zh: 乃具以其事白上。

translations.literal: He thereupon fully disclosed the affair to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He then revealed the whole affair to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上大驚，即遣收鸚鵡；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly shocked and immediately dispatched men to seize Yingwu;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was horrified and at once ordered Yingwu seized;

sentences.zh: 封籍其家，得劭、濬書數百紙，皆咒詛巫蠱之言；

translations.literal: sealed and inventoried her household, obtaining several hundred sheets of Shao's and Jun's writings, all words of cursing and witchcraft;
translations.idiomatic: sealed her household and found hundreds of letters from Shao and Jun—curses and witchcraft through and through;

sentences.zh: 又得所埋玉人，命有司窮治其事。

translations.literal: also obtained the buried jade figure and ordered the authorities to pursue the matter to the end.
translations.idiomatic: they also unearthed the buried jade effigy, and the emperor ordered a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 道育亡命，捕之不獲。

translations.literal: Daoyu fled for her life; she was sought but not captured.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu fled; despite pursuit she was not captured.

sentences.zh: 先是，濬自揚州剌史出鎮京口，及廬陵王紹以疾解揚州，意謂己必復得之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jun went out from Governor of Yangzhou to garrison Jingkou, and when Prince Shao of Luling by illness relinquished Yangzhou, he supposed he would surely regain it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jun had left the Yangzhou governorship to take up his post at Jingkou; when Prince Shao of Luling relinquished Yangzhou on account of illness, Jun assumed he would regain it.

sentences.zh: 既而上用南譙王義宣，濬殊不樂，乃求鎮江陵；

translations.literal: Yet the emperor employed Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao; Jun was deeply displeased and thereupon requested to garrison Jiangling;
