translations.idiomatic: Instead the emperor gave Yangzhou to Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao; Jun was bitterly disappointed and asked to hold Jiangling;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 濬入朝，遣還京口，為行留處分，至京口數日而巫蠱事發。

translations.literal: Jun entered court; he was sent back to Jingkou for arrangements of departure and stay; within a few days at Jingkou the witchcraft affair broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Jun came to court, was sent back to Jingkou for farewell arrangements, and within days the witchcraft scandal erupted.

sentences.zh: 上惋歎彌日，謂潘淑妃曰：「太子圖富貴，更是一理，虎頭復如此，非復思慮所及。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in regret for days and said to Consort Pan Shufei: "The crown prince scheming for wealth and honor is one thing; Tiger Head acting thus again is no longer within what can be pondered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned for days and told Consort Pan Shufei: "The crown prince plotting for power is one thing—but Tiger Head again! This is beyond anything I could have imagined.

sentences.zh: 汝母子豈可一日無我邪！」

translations.literal: You mother and son—can you go a single day without me!"
translations.idiomatic: Can you and your son survive a single day without me?"

sentences.zh: 遣中使切責劭、濬，劭、濬惶懼無辭，惟陳謝而已。

translations.literal: He sent a palace envoy to sternly reproach Shao and Jun; Shao and Jun were fearful and had no words, only offering apologies.
translations.idiomatic: He sent palace envoys to rebuke Shao and Jun harshly; terrified and speechless, they could only beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 上雖怒甚，猶未忍罪也。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was very angry, he still did not bear to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Furious though he was, the emperor still could not bring himself to punish them.

sentences.zh: 諸軍攻碻磝，治三攻道：張永等當東道，濟南太守申坦等當西道，揚武司馬崔訓當南道。

translations.literal: The various armies attacked Que'ao and constructed three assault routes: Zhang Yong and others held the eastern route, Shen Tan, Administrator of Jinan, and others the western route, Cui Xun, Major of Raised Martial the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: The armies assaulted Que'ao along three siege lines: Zhang Yong on the east, Administrator of Jinan Shen Tan on the west, and Raised Martial Major Cui Xun on the south.

sentences.zh: 攻之累旬，不拔。

translations.literal: They attacked for many tens of days and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: For weeks they assaulted the city without success.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛亥夜，魏人自地道潛出，燒崔訓營及攻具；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the night of xinhai, Wei men stole out through a tunnel, burned Cui Xun's camp and siege engines;
translations.idiomatic: On the night of xinhai in the eighth month, Wei troops emerged through a tunnel and burned Cui Xun's camp and siege equipment;

sentences.zh: 癸丑夜，又燒東圍及攻具；

translations.literal: on the night of guichou they again burned the eastern encirclement and siege engines;
translations.idiomatic: on the night of guichou they burned the eastern works and siege gear again;

sentences.zh: 尋復毀崔訓攻道。

translations.literal: before long they again destroyed Cui Xun's assault route.
translations.idiomatic: soon they wrecked Cui Xun's assault line as well.

sentences.zh: 張永夜撤圍退軍，不告諸將，士卒驚擾；

translations.literal: Zhang Yong by night withdrew the siege and retreated the army, not informing the generals; soldiers were startled and thrown into disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong withdrew by night without telling the other commanders; the troops panicked;

sentences.zh: 魏人乘之，死傷塗地。

translations.literal: the Wei seized the chance; dead and wounded covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei pressed the rout, and the slaughter was horrific.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話自往，增兵力攻旬餘，不拔。

translations.literal: Xiao Sihua went in person, added troops and attacked for more than ten days, and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua went in person, reinforced the assault for another ten days, and still could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 是時，青、徐不稔，軍食乏。

translations.literal: At this time Qing and Xu had poor harvests; army provisions were wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Xu had failed harvests that year, and army rations ran short.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，思話命諸軍皆退屯歷城，斬崔訓，系張永、申坦於獄。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Sihua ordered all armies to withdraw and encamp at Licheng, beheaded Cui Xun, and bound Zhang Yong and Shen Tan in prison.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Sihua ordered a general withdrawal to Licheng, executed Cui Xun, and imprisoned Zhang Yong and Shen Tan.

sentences.zh: 魯爽至長社，魏戍主禿髡幡棄城走。

translations.literal: Lu Shuang reached Changshe; the Wei garrison commander, Tufa Fan, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuang reached Changshe; the Wei commander Tufa Fan abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 臧質頓兵近郊，不以時發，獨遣冠軍司馬柳元景帥後軍行參軍薛安都等向潼關，元景等進據洪關。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi halted troops in the near suburbs and did not set out at the proper time; he alone dispatched Champion Major Liu Yuanjing to lead Rear Army Acting Commander Xue Andu and others toward Tong Pass; Yuanjing and the rest advanced and seized Hong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi camped his army in the suburbs and delayed his march; he sent only Champion Major Liu Yuanjing with Rear Army Acting Commander Xue Andu and others toward Tong Pass, and Yuanjing seized Hong Pass.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史劉秀之遣司馬馬汪與左軍中兵參軍蕭道成，將兵向長安。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuzhi, Governor of Liangzhou, dispatched Major Ma Wang and Left Army Central Arms Commander Xiao Daocheng to lead troops toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuzhi, Governor of Liangzhou, sent Major Ma Wang and Left Army Central Arms Commander Xiao Daocheng toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 道成，承之之子也。

translations.literal: Daocheng was the son of Xiao Chengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng was a son of Xiao Chengzhi.

sentences.zh: 魏冠軍將軍封禮自浢津南渡，赴弘農。

translations.literal: Feng Li, Wei Champion General, crossed south from Bozhou Ford to hurry to Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Champion General Feng Li crossed south from Bozhou Ford to relieve Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 九月，司空高平公兒烏干屯潼關，平南將軍黎公遼屯河內。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Er Wugan, Duke of Gaoping and Minister of Works, encamped at Tong Pass; Li Gongliao, General Who Pacifies the South, encamped in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Minister of Works Er Wugan, Duke of Gaoping, held Tong Pass, and General Who Pacifies the South Li Gongliao held Henei.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王慕利延卒，樹洛干之子拾寅立，始居伏羅川；

translations.literal: Murong Muliyan, king of Tuyuhun, died; Shiyin of Shulogan was established and first dwelt at Fuluo River;
translations.idiomatic: King Muliyan of Tuyuhun died; Shiyin, son of Shulogan, succeeded him and established his seat on the Fuluo River;

sentences.zh: 遣使來請命，亦請命於魏。

translations.literal: he dispatched envoys to request investiture and also requested investiture from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: he sent envoys to seek titles from both courts.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以拾寅為安西將軍、西秦、河、沙三州刺史、河南王；

translations.literal: On dinghai, Shiyin was made General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of the three provinces of Xiqin, He, and Sha, and Prince of Henan;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the Song appointed Shiyin General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Xiqin, He, and Sha, and Prince of Henan;

sentences.zh: 魏以拾寅為鎮西大將軍、沙州刺史、西平王。

translations.literal: Wei made Shiyin Grand General Who Guards the West, Inspector of Sha, and Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made him Grand General Who Guards the West, governor of Sha, and Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魯爽與魏豫州刺史拓跋僕蘭戰於大索，破之，進攻虎牢。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Lu Shuang battled Toba Pulán, Wei Inspector of Yuzhou, at Dasuo, defeated him, and advanced to attack Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Lu Shuang defeated Toba Pulán, Wei governor of Yuzhou, at Dasuo and pressed on to assault Hulao.

sentences.zh: 聞碻磝敗退，與柳元景皆引兵還。

translations.literal: On hearing of the defeat and withdrawal at Que'ao, he and Liu Yuanjing both drew back their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the rout at Que'ao, he and Liu Yuanjing both withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成、馬汪等聞魏救兵將至，還趣仇池。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng, Ma Wang, and the rest, hearing Wei relief troops were about to arrive, turned back toward Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng and Ma Wang, learning Wei reinforcements were near, retreated toward Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔解蕭思話徐州，更領冀州刺史，鎮歷城。

translations.literal: On jichou, an edict relieved Xiao Sihua of Xuzhou and had him again hold Jizhou Inspector, garrisoning Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou an edict transferred Xiao Sihua from Xuzhou to Jizhou and posted him at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 上以諸將屢出無功，不可專責張永等，賜思話詔曰：「虜既乘利，方向盛冬，若脫敢送死，兄弟父子自共當之耳。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the generals had repeatedly gone out without achievement, held it improper to blame Zhang Yong and others alone; he bestowed on Sihua an edict saying: "The barbarians having seized advantage, and the season turning toward deep winter—if perchance they dare come to die, brothers and fathers and sons will together answer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the commanders had failed again and again, the emperor would not blame Zhang Yong alone; he sent Sihua an edict: "The foe has the upper hand and winter is coming—if they dare offer battle, let them face us, fathers and sons together.

sentences.zh: 言及增憤！

translations.literal: To speak of it only increases rage!
translations.idiomatic: Even to speak of it fills me with rage!

sentences.zh: 可以示張永、申坦。」

translations.literal: You may show this to Zhang Yong and Shen Tan."
translations.idiomatic: Show this to Zhang Yong and Shen Tan."

sentences.zh: 又與江夏王義恭書曰：「早知諸將輩如此，恨不以白刃驅之。

translations.literal: He also wrote to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia: "Had I known earlier these generals would be thus, I regret not driving them with naked blades.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Prince Yigong of Jiangxia: "Had I known these commanders would fare so, I would have driven them with naked steel.

sentences.zh: 今者悔何所及！」

translations.literal: But now—what regret can still reach!"
translations.idiomatic: But now it is too late for regret!"

sentences.zh: 義恭尋奏免思話官，從之。

translations.literal: Yigong soon memorialized to dismiss Sihua from office; [the emperor] followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong soon memorialized to strip Sihua of his post; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 魏南安隱王余自以違次而立，厚賜群下，欲以收眾心；

translations.literal: Yu, Prince of Nan'an the Hidden of Wei, because he had been established in violation of succession order, lavished gifts on subordinates, wishing thereby to win hearts;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Nan'an, having been enthroned out of turn, lavished rewards on his followers to win their loyalty;

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，府藏虛竭。

translations.literal: Within a month's time, the treasury stores were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the palace treasury was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 又好酣飲及聲樂、畋獵，不恤政事。

translations.literal: He also loved deep drinking, music, and hunting, and did not care for state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also indulged in heavy drinking, music, and hunts, neglecting government.

sentences.zh: 宗愛為宰相，錄三省，總宿衛，坐召公卿，專恣日甚。

translations.literal: Zong Ai served as Chancellor, recorded the Three Departments, oversaw the palace guard, summoned ministers while seated, and grew daily more arbitrary.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ai was chancellor, controlled the Three Departments and the palace guard, summoned officials to audience while seated, and grew more domineering by the day.

sentences.zh: 余患之，謀奪其權；

translations.literal: Yu resented this and plotted to seize his power;
translations.idiomatic: Yu resented him and plotted to strip him of power;

sentences.zh: 愛憤怒。

translations.literal: Ai grew furious.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ai was enraged.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午朔，余夜祭東廟，愛使小黃門賈周等就弒余，而秘之，唯羽林郎中代人劉尼知之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the bingwu new moon, Yu at night sacrificed at the Eastern Temple; Ai sent the Junior Yellow Gate Jia Zhou and others to go and assassinate Yu, and kept it secret—only the Yulin Cadet Liu Ni of the Dai people knew.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day (bingwu), Yu offered night sacrifice at the Eastern Temple. Ai sent Junior Yellow Gate Jia Zhou and others to murder him and hushed it up; only Yulin Cadet Liu Ni of the Dai clan knew.

sentences.zh: 尼勸愛立皇孫濬，愛驚曰：「君大癡人！

translations.literal: Ni urged Ai to establish the imperial grandson Jun; Ai started and said: "Sir, you are a great fool!
translations.idiomatic: Ni urged Ai to enthrone the imperial grandson Jun. Ai cried out, "You utter fool!

sentences.zh: 皇孫若立，豈忘正平時事乎！」

translations.literal: If the imperial grandson is established, will he not remember the affairs of the Zhengping era!"
translations.idiomatic: If the grandson takes the throne, will he not remember what happened in the Zhengping years!"

sentences.zh: 尼曰：「若爾，今當立誰？」

translations.literal: Ni said: "If that is so, whom ought we establish now?"
translations.idiomatic: Ni asked, "If so, whom should we enthrone now?"

sentences.zh: 愛曰：「待還宮，當擇諸王賢者立之。」

translations.literal: Ai said: "Wait until we return to the palace, then we shall choose among the princes the worthy one and establish him."
translations.idiomatic: Ai said, "When we return to the palace, we will choose the ablest among the princes and enthrone him."

sentences.zh: 尼恐愛為變，密以狀告殿中尚書源賀。

translations.literal: Ni feared Ai would change course and secretly reported the facts to Palace Attendant Yuan He.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful that Ai might change plans, Ni secretly informed Palace Attendant Yuan He.

sentences.zh: 賀時與尼俱典兵宿衛，乃與南部尚書陸麗謀曰：「宗愛既立南安，還復殺之。

translations.literal: He at the time together with Ni commanded troops on palace guard, and thereupon with Southern Department Minister Lu Li plotted, saying: "Zong Ai having established Nan'an, again killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then on guard duty with Ni; together with Southern Department Minister Lu Li he said, "Zong Ai set up Nan'an and then killed him.

sentences.zh: 今又不立皇孫，將不利於社稷。」

translations.literal: Now he again will not establish the imperial grandson—this will be harmful to the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Now he refuses the imperial grandson too—the realm is in peril."

sentences.zh: 遂與麗定謀，共立皇孫。

translations.literal: They thereupon fixed a plot with Li and together established the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: They settled on a coup with Li to enthrone the grandson.

sentences.zh: 麗，俟之子也。

translations.literal: Li was the son of Hou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Li was the son of Tuoba Hou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，賀與尚書長孫渴侯嚴兵守衛宮禁，使尼、麗迎皇孫於苑中。

translations.literal: On wushen, He together with Minister Changsun Kehou rigorously armed troops to guard the palace precincts, and sent Ni and Li to welcome the imperial grandson in the park.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Yuan He and Minister Changsun Kehou mustered troops to secure the palace and sent Ni and Li to fetch the grandson from the park.

sentences.zh: 麗抱皇孫於馬上，入平城，賀、渴侯開門納之。

translations.literal: Li embraced the imperial grandson on the horse, entered Pingcheng; He and Kehou opened the gate and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Li carried the grandson on horseback into Pingcheng; He and Kehou opened the gates to admit them.

sentences.zh: 尼馳還東廟，大呼曰：「宗愛弒南安王，大逆不道，皇孫已登大位，有詔，宿衛之士皆還宮！」

translations.literal: Ni galloped back to the Eastern Temple and shouted greatly: "Zong Ai assassinated the Prince of Nan'an—great treason and impiety! The imperial grandson has already ascended the Great Position. There is an edict: all palace guard troops return to the palace!"
translations.idiomatic: Ni raced back to the Eastern Temple and shouted, "Zong Ai murdered Prince Nan'an—treason of the worst kind! The imperial grandson is already emperor. By edict: all guards return to the palace!"

sentences.zh: 眾鹹呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The masses all shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The troops all cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 遂執宗愛、賈周等，勒兵而入，奉皇孫即皇帝位。

translations.literal: They thereupon seized Zong Ai, Jia Zhou, and others, compelled troops to enter, and installed the imperial grandson as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Zong Ai, Jia Zhou, and the rest, marched in with armed men, and enthroned the grandson as emperor.

sentences.zh: 登永安殿，大赦，改元興安。

translations.literal: He ascended Yong'an Hall, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name to Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: He took the throne in Yong'an Hall, declared a general amnesty, and proclaimed the Xing'an era.

sentences.zh: 殺愛、周，皆具五刑，夷三族。

translations.literal: They killed Ai and Zhou; both received the full five punishments, and their three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Ai and Zhou were executed with the full five punishments, and their kin to the third degree were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 西陽五水群蠻反，自淮、汝至於江、沔，鹹被其患。

translations.literal: The Five-Water tribal confederation of Xiyang rebelled; from the Huai and Ru to the Yangtze and Han, all alike suffered their harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Five-Water tribes of Xiyang rose in revolt; from the Huai and Ru to the Yangtze and Han, the region suffered their raids.

sentences.zh: 詔太尉中兵參軍沈慶之督江、豫、荊、雍四州兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Marshal Staff Officer Shen Qingzhi to supervise the troops of Jiang, Yu, Jing, and Yong four provinces to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Grand Marshal staff officer Shen Qingzhi to command the forces of Jiang, Yu, Jing, and Yong and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 魏以驃騎大將軍拓跋壽樂為太宰、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，長孫渴侯為尚書令，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wei made General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry Tuoba Shoule Grand Mentor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; Changsun Kehou Minister-in-Chief, with added Three Excellencies Equal in Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry Tuoba Shoule Grand Mentor, supreme commander, and head of the secretariat; Changsun Kehou became Minister-in-Chief with ceremonial three-department rank.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壽樂、渴侯坐爭權，並賜死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Shoule and Kehou on account of struggling for power were both granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Shoule and Kehou were both ordered to commit suicide for fighting over power.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏廣陽簡王建、臨淮宣王譚皆卒。

translations.literal: On guiwei, both Jian, Prince of Guangyang the Plain, and Xuan, Prince of Linhuai, Tan, died.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Jian, Prince of Guangyang, and Tan, Prince of Linhuai, both died.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏主母閭氏卒。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Wei ruler's mother, Lady Lu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Wei emperor's mother, Lady Lu, died.

sentences.zh: 魏南安王余之立也，以古弼為司徒，張黎為太尉。

translations.literal: When Yu, Prince of Nan'an of Wei, was established, they made Gu Bi Minister of Works and Zhang Li Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Nan'an was enthroned, Gu Bi was made Minister of Works and Zhang Li Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及高宗立，弼、黎議不合旨，黜為外都大官；

translations.literal: When Gaozong was established, Bi and Li's deliberations did not accord with the imperial intent; they were demoted to Outer Capital Grand Officials;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, Gu Bi and Zhang Li fell out of favor and were demoted to outer-court grand officers;

sentences.zh: 坐有怨言，且家人告其為巫蠱，皆被誅。

translations.literal: On account of harboring complaints, and moreover because family members reported them for witchcraft charms, both were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of disloyal talk and witchcraft by their own households, they were both executed.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，廬陵昭王紹卒。

translations.literal: On renyin, Shao, Prince Zhao of Luling, died.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Prince Shao of Luling died.

sentences.zh: 魏追尊景穆太子為景穆皇帝，皇妣閭氏為恭皇后，尊乳母常氏為保太后。

translations.literal: Wei posthumously honored the Crown Prince Jingmu as Emperor Jingmu, the imperial mother Lady Lu as Empress Gong, and honored wet-nurse Lady Chang as Dowager Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Wei posthumously ennobled Crown Prince Jingmu as Emperor Jingmu, his mother Lady Lu as Empress Gong, and his nurse Lady Chang as Protector Dowager.

sentences.zh: 隴西屠各王景文叛魏，署置王侯；

translations.literal: Jingwen, king of the Tuge of Longxi, rebelled against Wei and appointed kings and marquises;
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen, king of the Tuge in Longxi, rebelled against Wei and installed his own kings and lords;

sentences.zh: 魏統萬鎮將南陽王惠壽、外都大官於洛拔督四州之眾討平之，徙其黨三千餘家於趙、魏。

translations.literal: Wei's Tongwan Garrison General, Prince of Nanyang Huishou, and Outer Capital Grand Official Yu Luoba directed the masses of four provinces to suppress and pacify them, and moved more than three thousand households of their partisans to Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei generals Huishou of Nanyang and Yu Luoba led forces from four provinces to crush the revolt and relocated more than three thousand rebel households to Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊申，魏葬恭皇后於金陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wushen, Wei buried Empress Gong at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wushen, Wei buried Empress Gong at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 魏世祖晚年，佛禁稍弛，民間往往有私習者。

translations.literal: In Wei Emperor Shizu's later years, the Buddhist prohibition gradually slackened; among the people there were often those who privately practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taiwu's last years, the ban on Buddhism had eased, and many practiced it in secret.

sentences.zh: 及高宗即位，群臣多請復之。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, many among the ministers requested its restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencheng came to the throne, many officials urged that the ban be lifted.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔州郡縣眾居之所，各聽建佛圖一區；

translations.literal: On yimao, an edict: in every place where the masses dwell in prefectures, districts, and counties, each was permitted to build one Buddhist shrine compound;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, an edict allowed one Buddhist temple per county seat and major settlement;

sentences.zh: 民欲為沙門者，聽出家。

translations.literal: Commoners who wished to become shramanas were permitted to leave the household.
translations.idiomatic: and those who wished to take monastic vows were allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 大州五十人，小州四十人。

translations.literal: Large prefectures fifty persons, small prefectures forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Large prefectures could ordain fifty monks; small prefectures, forty.

sentences.zh: 於是向所毀佛圖，率皆修復。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Buddha shrines previously destroyed were, for the most part, all restored.
translations.idiomatic: The temples destroyed in the persecution were largely rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 魏主親為沙門師賢等五人下髮，以師賢為道人統。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler personally cut the hair for the shramana Shixian and four others, and made Shixian Director of the Daoist Masters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally tonsured five monks including Shixian and appointed Shixian chief of the clergy.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏以樂陵王擊忸為太尉，南部尚書陸麗為司徒，鎮西將軍杜元寶為司空。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Wei made Prince of Leiling Ji Ni Grand Marshal, Southern Department Minister Lu Li Minister of Works, and Pacification-of-the-West General Du Yuanbao Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Wei named Prince of Leiling Ji Ni Grand Marshal, Lu Li Minister of Works, and Du Yuanbao Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 麗以迎立之功，受心膂之寄，朝臣無出其右者，賜爵平原王。

translations.literal: Li because of the merit of welcoming and establishing [the emperor], received the trust of the heart and backbone; among court ministers none surpassed him—he was granted the title King of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: For installing the emperor, Lu Li became the emperor's most trusted minister and was enfeoffed as King of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 麗辭曰：「陛下，國之正統，當承基緒；

translations.literal: Li declined, saying: "Your Majesty is the state's orthodox line; you ought to inherit the foundation and succession;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Li declined: "Your Majesty is the legitimate heir and rightfully holds the throne;

sentences.zh: 效順奉迎，臣子常職，不敢慆天之功以干大賞。」

translations.literal: Rendering loyalty in welcoming and attending is a subject's constant duty—I dare not lay hold of Heaven's merit to encroach upon a great reward."
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming you was a subject's plain duty; I dare not claim heaven's credit to demand grand rewards."

sentences.zh: 再三不受，魏主不許。

translations.literal: Three times he declined and would not accept; the Wei ruler would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused three times; the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 麗曰：「臣父奉事先朝，忠勤著效。

translations.literal: Li said: "My father served the previous court, his loyalty and diligence manifest in achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Li said, "My father served the previous reign with loyal, distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 今年逼桑榆，願以臣爵授之。」

translations.literal: This year he nears the mulberry and elms; I wish to confer my ennoblement upon him."
translations.idiomatic: He is at life's evening; let me give him my title."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕為天下主，豈不能使卿父子為二王邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I am lord of all under Heaven—can I not make you father and son two kings!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I rule the realm—can I not make you and your father both kings?"

sentences.zh: 戊午，進其父建業公俟爵為東平王。

translations.literal: On wuwu, he advanced his father, the Duke of Jianye, Hou's rank to King of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he enfeoffed Lu Li's father Hou as King of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 又命麗妻為妃，復其子孫。

translations.literal: He also ordered Li's wife to be made consort and restored his sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lu Li's wife a consort and restored his sons and grandsons to favor.

sentences.zh: 麗力辭不受，帝益嘉之。

translations.literal: Li vigorously declined and would not accept; the emperor all the more praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Li firmly declined; the emperor admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 以東安公劉尼為尚書僕射，西平公源賀為征北將軍，並進爵為王。

translations.literal: They made Duke of Dong'an Liu Ni Deputy Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Duke of Xiping Yuan He General Who Pacifies the North; both advanced in rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni was made Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Yuan He General Who Pacifies the North; both were promoted to prince.

sentences.zh: 帝班賜群臣，謂源賀曰：「卿任意取之。」

translations.literal: The emperor distributed rewards to the ministers and said to Yuan He: "You may take as you wish."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed out gifts and told Yuan He, "Take whatever you like."

sentences.zh: 賀辭曰：「南北未賓，府庫不可虛也。」

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "North and south have not yet submitted; the treasury must not be emptied."
translations.idiomatic: He refused: "North and south are still unsubdued; the treasury cannot be emptied."

sentences.zh: 固與之，乃取戎馬一匹。

translations.literal: He firmly urged it upon him; only then did he take one war horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor insisted; Yuan He took a single warhorse.

sentences.zh: 高宗之立也，高允預其謀，陸麗等皆受重賞，而不及允，允終身不言。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was established, Gao Yun had foreknown the plot; Lu Li and the rest all received heavy rewards, but Yun was not included—Yun never spoke of it in his whole life.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun had helped plan Wencheng's accession, yet while Lu Li and others were richly rewarded, Yun received nothing—and never mentioned it again.

sentences.zh: 甲子，周忸坐事賜死。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zhou Ni on account of an affair was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Ji Ni was ordered to commit suicide for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 時魏法深峻，源賀奏：「謀反之家，男子十三以下本不預謀者，宜免死沒官。」

translations.literal: At this time Wei law was deep and severe; Yuan He memorialized: "In families guilty of rebellion, males thirteen and below who originally did not participate in the plot ought to be spared death and become government slaves."
translations.idiomatic: With Wei law still harsh, Yuan He proposed: "In treason cases, boys thirteen and under who took no part in plotting should be spared execution and enslaved to the state instead."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭還朝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia returned to court.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以義恭為大將軍、南徐州刺史，錄尚書如故。

translations.literal: On xinwei, they made Yigong Grand General and Inspector of South Xuzhou, recording the Masters of Writing as before.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he was named Grand General, Inspector of South Xuzhou, and continued as recorder of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，魏入中原，用《景初曆》，世祖克沮渠氏，得趙𢾺《玄始曆》，時人以為密，是歲，始行之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Wei entered the Central Plains, they used the Jingchu Calendar; Shizu conquered the Juqu clan and obtained Zhao 𢾺's Xuanshi Calendar, which men of the time deemed precise; this year, they began to employ it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei first entered the Central Plains they had used the Jingchu calendar; after Taiwu conquered the Juqu, he obtained Zhao 𢾺's Xuanshi calendar, which was esteemed as more accurate, and this year it was put into use.
